english: The heart rejoices through wine. Drink wine with a friend. Do not deceive him. Let them give him your share. A dog is dear to the shepherd. A man of ill fame is not dear (friendly).
uncertain: CONTAMINATION: a format-check command accidentally printed this item's English field before translation; this rendering is not blind
wih₁néh₁: INS.SG of wéyh₁ō 'wine' -> 'through/with wine'
méwdt: AOR.3SG 'became joyful', read as gnomic present
ḱéywoh₁: INS.SG 'with a friend' after ḱóm (also NOM/ACC.DU 'two friends')
dh₃éntu: IMP.3PL 'let them give', a 3PL subject in a run of 2SG commands (ph₃dʰí, mē dʰrugʰyés); a 2SG imperative would fit the context
dusḱléwēs: compound dus- + ḱléwes-, read NOM.SG 'ill-famed'

english: A sheep on which there was no wool saw horses: one pulling a heavy wagon, one (carrying) a great load, one carrying a man swiftly.
uncertain: h₂wlh₂néh₂: spelled with h₂ where the lexicon has h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ 'wool'; read as 'wool'
(H)yésmin: relative LOC.SG 'on which', with parenthesized laryngeal
dedorḱe: perfect 'has seen', read as narrative past 'saw'
tóm ... tóm ... tóm: ACC.SG 'that one', distributive over h₁éḱwons; second clause has no verb ('carrying' supplied from bʰérontm)
h₂oHḱú: adverb 'swiftly'

english: Father, you led us and gave us horses. You protected us; we remember you. Frost seized us; now we sit and weep. Now who speaks to us and leads us?
uncertain: nos: enclitic ACC/DAT/GEN.PL; read as object of déwks, indirect object of dédeh₃s, object of h₂lékses
déwks/dédeh₃s/h₂lékses: 2SG past forms, all 'you'
lémbʰt: AOR.3SG with subject sríHgos 'frost'
bʰéh₂ti nos: 'speaks to us' (nos as dative) or 'speaks of us'

english: Work! Plough the field. He who ploughs, he eats. Milk the cows. Build the enclosure. Yoke the horses. He who works receives his own share.
uncertain: gʷṓs: read ACC.PL 'cows'; the same form is NOM.SG 'cow'
déme: IMP.2SG of dem- 'build' (not demh₂- 'tame'); 'build/fence the enclosure'
h₁áyto: MID.AOR.3SG 'took/received', read as gnomic
swóm: reflexive possessive 'his own'

english: "I want a son."
uncertain: wēlh₁mi: 1SG present of welh₁- 'want/choose', not found as a lexicon cell; 'I want/choose'
súHnum: ACC.SG 'son'; context (who speaks) unknown

english: Old father, you died; you saw many years. You knew the words of the old. You led us, you sat (with us), and you spoke to us. Now the gods have received you; your name is famous.
uncertain: mérs: AOR.2SG of mer- 'die' or of mers- 'forget'; read 'you died' given the funeral context (alternative: 'you forgot')
mérs ... widés: two finite verbs with no conjunction
yéh₁ōr: NOM/ACC.PL 'years' with polh₁úh₂ (neuter plural 'many')
ǵn̥néh₃s: PST.2SG 'you knew/recognized'; nu 'now' sits oddly with a past verb
wédʰes: PST.2SG of wedʰ- 'lead' (or wedʰ- 'bind'); read 'you led us'
h₁áyn̥to: MID.AOR.3PL 'received/took', subject deywṓs NOM.PL
ḱlutóm: read as adjective 'famous' agreeing with h₁nómn̥ (also IMP.2DU 'hear!')

english: (You) two sons, hear me! A brother is dear. Do not (you two) leave your brother. Two brothers are strong. Eat together, drink together. Whoever leaves him is a wolf.
uncertain: súHnuh₁: NOM/VOC.DU 'two sons', read as vocative
ḱlutóm: IMP.2DU 'hear!' (also ACC.SG 'famous')
téwe: GEN.SG 'your (singular)', addressing two sons with dual verbs (linkʷtóm, h₁édtom, píph₃etom); a dual possessive would be expected
linkʷtóm/h₁édtom/píph₃etom: 2DU imperative (or injunctive) forms
steh₂róh₁: dual 'strong/stout'; the lexicon also glosses it 'big; old'
h₁ím: 'him' = the brother

english: Protect your oath. The oath is great. Do not break the oath. Father Dyeus sees. Whoever breaks the oath, Perkwunos strikes him. Whoever keeps the oath, his name is famous.
uncertain: bʰoydʰéh₂: 'pledge, oath, contract'
mē Hrunéps: PST.2SG injunctive with prohibitive
dedórḱe: perfect 'has seen' read as present 'sees'
méǵh₂ih₂: feminine 'great', agreeing with bʰoydʰéh₂; not found as a lexicon cell

english: Serpent, lie down! Do not seize this man. Serpent, you who crawl at night, do not rise up. Perkwunos, strike the serpent for yourself with the spear. Serpent, flee! Now let the serpent go away.
uncertain: ḱóm wiHróm: ḱóm read as ACC.SG of deictic 'this' ('this man'); it could also be the preposition 'with' ('do not seize (anything) with the man'), which does not fit
h₁yós ... sérpesi: relative with a 2SG verb, 'you who crawl'
stéh₂s: AOR.2SG injunctive 'do not stand up/rise'
toy: enclitic DAT/GEN 2SG, 'for you/yourself' (ethic dative) or 'your serpent'
ǵʰoysóh₁: INS.SG 'with the spear', or ACC.DU 'two spears'
final sentence moves from 2SG address (bʰugdʰí) to 3SG imperative (léyttu) with h₁ógʷʰis as NOM

english: Heart, do not tremble; heart, do not fear. Anguish, go out of the heart! Dawn and Sun, drive (you two) the anguish out of the heart. Now may sleep come to him. May the tears dry up, and now may he rejoice.
uncertain: ḱḗr: NOM/ACC form used as vocative
tréms/bʰéyh₂s: 2SG past forms used as prohibitive injunctives
h₂éwsos: short-vowel spelling where the lexicon NOM is h₂éwsōs 'Dawn'; read as Dawn
h₁l̥h₂tóm: 2DU imperative 'drive', addressed to Dawn and Sun; ḱr̥dés as ablative without h₁éǵʰs
h₁ésmey 'to him': no 3rd-person referent; the heart was addressed in the 2nd person
dáḱruh₂: neuter plural 'tears' with 3SG verb tr̥syéh₁t (collective agreement)
mudyéh₁t: 3SG optative 'may he/it rejoice', subject unclear (the man? the heart?)

english: He who drove you two, the two swift horses, is dead. You stand at the yoke, and nobody yoked you two. Now you two horses seek him. The two horses do not eat; the chariot stands still.
uncertain: uh₃wé: 2nd-person ACC.DU 'you two'; HéHḱuh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁ in apposition (VOC/ACC.DU)
h₂éǵet: PST.3SG 'drove'
stesth₂é: PRF.2PL in the paradigm, plural, while the horses are dual elsewhere (uh₃wé, h₁éḱwoh₁, 2/3DU verbs); a dual is expected
yugóy: LOC.SG 'at the yoke' (also NOM/ACC.DU)
kʷis ne: indefinite 'anyone ... not' = 'nobody'
h₂isḱétes/h₁édtes: 2DU or 3DU; read 2DU 'you two seek' in the first case and 3DU 'the two horses do not eat' in the second
kʷékʷlos: 'wheel/chariot'; stestóh₂e PRF.3SG 'has come to a stand'

english: Son, do not die; live and grow! Your mother protects you. May Dyeus and Earth (the two) protect you. Now let anguish go to the wolf. Let the beast eat it; Death, pass him by. Dyeus, giver of good things, give him power.
uncertain: mē mérs: AOR.2SG of mer- 'die' (or mers- 'forget'); read 'do not die'
ph₂sih₁tā́m: OPT.3DU 'may the two protect', subject Dyeus and Earth
wĺ̥kʷom: ACC.SG as goal, 'to the wolf'
h₁íd 'it' = the anguish (neuter h₂énǵʰos)
gʷh₂te: VOC of gʷh₂tós 'death'; dʰgʷʰh₂dʰí 'pass by'
h₁uséwōm: GEN.PL 'of good things'; séǵʰos 'power, control'
h₁ésmey/h₁ím 'him' = the son, now in the 3rd person after 2nd-person address

english: Dead shepherd, you lie in the field. Your dog sits and weeps. Now it is growing dark; the sheep do not eat. The wolf comes, and nobody guards them. Your name is famous among men.
uncertain: mŕ̥we: VOC 'dead (one)'; ḱéyth₂er MID.PRS.2SG 'you lie'
ḱwṓ: NOM.SG 'dog', but sédyetes is 2DU/3DU while HréwdHti is 3SG; the number of the verbs does not agree
toy: 'your' (enclitic GEN/DAT)
h₁íh₂n̥s: feminine ACC.PL 'them' = the sheep
h₂nr̥sú: LOC.PL 'among men'

english: Fire, water: run in the bones! May it cool in the bone; let frost come. Let the heat flee; let him sweat. Let him drink and be sated; may he not tremble.
uncertain: péh₂wr̥ wódr̥: both NOM/VOC neuter, but dr̥mdʰí is 2SG; unclear who is addressed (fire? water? 'fire, (become) water'?)
h₁íd ... studyéh₁t: OPT.3SG of stewd- 'become cold' with neuter 'it' (the fire/fever?) as subject; also homophonous with stewd- 'push'
gʷʰr̥nós: 'something warm, heat'
swidyétu/péh₃tu/térptu/trésoyh₁t: 3SG with no stated subject; read as the patient

english: Blood, stand! Blood, do not go out. The spear that wounded you, may it be broken. May the red blood stay in the sinew. Hear, father Dyeus, this word. Protect him, and may he grow strong.
uncertain: h₁yós ǵʰoysós ... só: relative-correlative, 'which spear ... it'
Hrumpih₁tó: MID.OPT.3SG 'may it be broken'
h₁rudʰéh₁n̥t: the paradigm gives PST.3PL 'they were red', which does not fit; read as an attributive participle 'red' with kréwh₂s
sth₂éh₁yoyh₁t: OPT.3SG 'may it stand/stay'
ḱód: neuter of deictic ḱí- 'this'
h₁ím/h₁éy 'him/he': the wounded man, previously addressed as 'you' (twé)

english: Give water and wine to the guest. He came from the sky (by day?). Do not deceive him. Seat him at your table. Do not drive him out of your home. The household that gives to the guest is dear to the gods. The guest remembers the givers.
uncertain: diwés: GEN/ABL.SG of Dyēws, 'from the sky/heaven' or temporal genitive 'by day'
h₁éy: NOM.SG 'he' (also IMP.2SG 'go!')
stóloy: LOC.SG 'at the table/seat'
h₁yós ḱóymos: ḱóymos is 'kin, homely' (adj.) or 'village, household'; read 'the household (member) who gives'
dh₃tr̥bʰós: DAT/ABL.PL with memóne 'remembers'; an ACC/GEN object would be expected, so the sense may be 'is mindful for the givers'

english: Wolf, do not seize the lamb; dog, guard the livestock. Shepherd, lead the cows home. May the wild beast not come near (in front). May wool grow; dog, keep watch. Now may the sheep be filled.
uncertain: ḱwón: VOC.SG 'dog'
ḱóymom: ACC.SG as goal, 'home/to the village'
h₂énti: LOC 'in front, facing', meaning in context uncertain ('come before (us)'?)
h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ bʰuHyóyh₁t: 'may wool grow/appear'
pl̥h₁ih₁ént: OPT.3PL of pleh₁- 'become full'

english: Husband, where did you go away? I went down to Mother Earth. Now who drives your cows? My brother-in-law drives them. Now who speaks words to you? The king speaks them. What do you carry? I carry imperishable fame; it does not die.
uncertain: wíHre: VOC 'man/husband'
gʷā́m: AOR.1SG 'I went' (homophonous with ACC.SG 'cow'); dʰéǵʰōm méh₂term̥ ACC of goal
toy: 'your' or 'to you'
swēḱurós: lexicon 'brother-in-law' (could be 'father-in-law'); méne GEN 'my'
h₁íh₂: FEM NOM.SG 'she' or neuter ACC.PL 'them'; read as neuter plural 'them (the words)'
h₁íd ne mr̥yétor: neuter 'it' (the fame)

english: Brother, I saw you falling. I stood in front and did not protect you. I carried you from the field; the field drank your blood. Now I go away and remember you. Your fame indeed is imperishable.
uncertain: sn̥gʷóntm̥: not found in the paradigms; read as ACC.SG participle of sengʷ- 'sink/fall'
widóm/h₂léksom/bʰérom: 1SG past forms
h₂énti: LOC 'in front' (adverbial)
stestóh₂h₂e/memónh₂e: PRF.1SG
-ge: emphatic particle

english: Son, hear my word. A true word is good. Speak the truth. Do not deceive a friend. He who speaks the truth is dear to the gods. The word that has gone out does not come back. Listen, then speak.
uncertain: méne: GEN.SG 'my' (also IMP.2SG of 'think')
h₁sónt: neuter of h₁sónts 'true', attributive in 'true word' and a noun 'the truth' elsewhere
h₁wésu: neuter 'good'
h₁yód ... tód: relative-correlative 'the word that ... it'; gʷéh₂t AOR.3SG
h₂ew: 'back, again'

english: Well-famed son, swift one! You did not grow old; you ran, and a spear wounded you. Red blood is in the field. Now we do not see you. Death took you; your name is famous.
uncertain: h₁súḱlewes/HéHḱew: vocatives
ǵorh₂éyeth₂e: MID.PST.2SG of the causative 'make old'; read as 'you were not made old' = 'you did not grow old'
dréms: AOR.2SG 'you ran'
h₁rudʰéh₁n̥t: the paradigm gives PST.3PL 'they were red', which does not fit; read as an adjective/participle 'red' with kréwh₂s
widéh₁yomes: PRS.1PL 'we see'

english: Give worship to the gods. They are givers of good things. The libation is dear to them. They have seen the giver. Father Dyeus hears the giver. Do not deceive the gods. Mother Earth carries men.
uncertain: némos: 'worship, sacrifice, bowing'
tóy: NOM.PL 'they' (the gods); no copula
ǵʰutóm: ACC/NOM.SG 'the libation (that which is poured)'; also IMP.2DU 'pour!'
dedr̥ḱḗr: PRF.3PL 'have seen'; déh₃torm̥ ACC.SG 'giver'
ḱléwseti: 'listens to/hears'
bʰéreti: 'carries/bears' (could also mean 'brings forth')

english: Now bone, blood and sinew: may bone be joined with bone, and blood be joined with blood; may sinew be joined with sinew. The bone that was broken, may it stand again. Earth mother, take the pain out of the bone. He who lies (here), let him stand up and walk.
uncertain: h₃sth₁éh₁/h₁sh₂énh₁/sn̥h₁wénh₁: INS.SG 'with/to bone/blood/sinew'
yungih₁tó: MID.OPT.3SG 'may it be joined'
Hrumptó: not in the paradigms; read as middle past 3SG 'was broken' of the nasal present Hrunép-
dʰéǵʰom méh₂ter: VOC; h₁áyso MID.IMP.2SG 'take (away)'
ḱéyor: MID.PRS.3SG 'lies'

english: He who lives, dies. The dead do not come back. Death took the old and the swift. Do not weep for many nights. The grief has gone away, and the sun comes.
uncertain: h₁áyto: MID.AOR.3SG 'took', gnomic or past
pl̥h₁éwih₂n̥s: not in the paradigms; read as feminine ACC.PL 'many' agreeing with kʷsépn̥s 'nights' (accusative of duration)
mē HréwdHs: PST.2SG injunctive with prohibitive
léytt: AOR.3SG 'went away'

english: The horses then said: "Listen, sheep! We see this, and our heart is pained: man, the master, makes the sheep's wool into a warm garment for himself, and the sheep have no wool."
uncertain: tu: particle 'then/and'
wewkond: 3PL past of wewk-/wekʷ- 'say'; not found as a cell
h₂owey: VOC.SG 'sheep', but the horses speak to the sheep as one
n̥sméy agʰnutór ḱḗr: DAT.PL 'for us' + middle 'is pained', 'the heart is pained for us'
sē: reflexive 'for himself' (form not in closed-class tables, which list sébʰye/soy)
h₂áwyes, h₂wl̥h₁náh₂, h₂áwibʰyos: a-vocalism spellings differ from lexicon h₂ówis/h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂; read GEN.SG 'of the sheep', ACC 'wool', DAT.PL 'to the sheep'
wept: AOR.3SG 'made/wove', read as gnomic 'makes'
closing quotation mark missing in the PIE

english: Swelling, do not grow; swelling, go down. Now, swelling, melt away. Let water carry the swelling away. Let frost seize the swelling. Let the beast swallow the swelling; let him live.
uncertain: péyh₂wr̥: lexicon 'fat; swelling', distinct from péh₂wr̥ 'fire'; if 'fire' was meant, the text means 'fire, do not increase ... let water carry the fire away'
pléh₁dʰes: PST.2SG injunctive of pléh₁dʰeti 'become full, swell, increase'
ní gʷh₂dʰí: 'go down'
tinh₁dʰí: IMP.2SG of tinéh₁ti 'melt, thaw; stop'
gʷíh₃wetu: 3SG imperative with no subject; read as the patient ('let him live'), though grammatically it could be the beast

english: Water goes down; from the fires (?) it goes up. Fire and water are not friends. The sun goes, and night comes. Night hides the thief. Dawn follows her.
uncertain: ph₂wénbʰos: DAT/ABL.PL of péh₂wr̥ 'fire', not NOM.SG; 'fire goes up' was probably meant, but the form reads 'out of/for the fires it goes up'
ḱéywoyh₁: NOM.DU neuter of ḱéywos 'friendly' (not a cell in the masculine paradigm)
bʰórm̥: ACC.SG of bʰṓr 'thief'
h₁íh₂m̥: FEM ACC.SG 'her' = night

english: Worm, you who eat bone, die! Worm, you who drink blood, let them perish! Now let fire burn you. Let the sun dry you. May the bird seize you; come out of the sinew! Come out of the bone; do not devour the sinew.
uncertain: kʷŕ̥mey: VOC.SG 'worm'; h₁yós with 2SG verbs = 'you who'
n̥ḱéntu: IMP.3PL 'let them perish/vanish' after a singular vocative; 2SG (like mr̥dʰí) expected
h₁pyéh₁t: OPT.3SG of h₁ep- 'seize'
sn̥h₁wéns/h₃sth₁és: ABL.SG 'out of sinew/bone' (with or without h₁éǵʰs)
h₁n̥dʰdʰí: IMP.2SG of h₁nedʰ- 'come forth'
gʷr̥h₃és: PST.2SG injunctive 'devour'
